conservation.condition_narrative:
1. The dark purple-brown paint scuff was reduced as much as possible using tiny swabs with acetone. Orange paint scuffs in the bottom right corner were removed in the same way with petroleum benzine. 
2. The remaining bits of purple-brown paint and small losses from the gouge in the bottom right corner were inpainted using dry pigments mixed in MS2A with Stoddards solvent. 
All the work was done under the stereomicroscope. 
The treatment was documented with color slides. 
Conservator: Besty Court 
Conservation Technician: Erick Gude 
Dates of Treatment: November 30 and December 1, 2004 
MS2A: modified polycyclohexanone reduced ketone resin (Linden Nazareth, U.K.)

remarks_post_1999: Lynes publication lists this work with a purchase date of “1970s”, yet the recto (cat. No. 450) is listed with a purchase date of 1964. A label on the backing of this object dates an exhibition showing at the Pasadena Art Museum in 1964 with the lender listed as “Ms. Jacqueline Greber.” This object was purchased sometime between 1946 (MoMA exhibition) and 1964 by Jacqueline Greber. Jacqueline Greber remarried at some point after 1964, and her last name changed to Wolber. (Source: UNM Art Museum, 2025)

description: This painting is on the back of *Portrait of a Day – 3rd Day*, 1924 (cat. no. 450).  Curved forms in shades of red, blue, purple, and white span the width of the canvas, overlapping one another to form concentric circles.
